Cylindrical capacitor · Gauss's law
Region
Guided demo
Display
The cut-away end is nearest the viewer (lower left); the far end carries the R₁ / r / R₂ callouts. Drag to orbit — the orange dashed cylinder nests between the two conductors along the whole length.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional cutaway of a cylindrical capacitor drawn in perspective, extending from the near end at the lower left toward the far end at the upper right. Two concentric conducting cylinders share a common axis: a narrow inner cylinder whose visible near face is crowded with plus signs, and a much wider outer shell whose surface carries minus signs spaced along its length and around its near rim. In the near end view, short red arrows labeled 'E' radiate outward from the inner cylinder across the annular gap to the inner wall of the outer shell, filling the gap uniformly in every radial direction. An orange dashed cylinder of intermediate radius is drawn between the two conductors, appearing as dashed ellipses at both ends joined by dashed lines running the length of the device; a curved leader from the top labels it 'Gaussian surface'. At the far end three arrows fan out from a point on the axis, labeled 'R1', 'r', and 'R2' in order of increasing length. Nesting the dashed surface between the two conductor radii shows precisely which charge it encloses. The geometry sets up the flux calculation that gives the capacitance of a coaxial pair carrying charges plus Q and minus Q.

elements: long outer conducting cylindrical shell (translucent bluish-grey), axis running from near lower-left to far upper-right
near-end annular face of the outer shell (visible ring, darker blue-grey)
inner solid conducting cylinder (narrow, coaxial, extends full length)
near-end circular face of the inner cylinder crowded with '+' signs
'+' signs distributed along the inner cylinder's visible length inside the cutaway
'−' signs distributed over the outer shell surface (along the length and around the near rim)
red radial E-field arrows in the annular gap at the near end, pointing outward from inner cylinder to outer shell
label 'E' near the top red arrow at the near end
orange dashed Gaussian cylinder of intermediate radius r, coaxial with the conductors
orange dashed ellipse at near end of Gaussian surface
orange dashed ellipse at far end of Gaussian surface
two orange dashed straight lines (top and bottom) joining the two dashed ellipses along the length
curved black leader arrow from the top-right text to the Gaussian surface
text label 'Gaussian surface'
three black radius arrows at the far end fanning from the axis point: R1 (to inner cylinder), r (to dashed surface), R2 (to outer shell)
labels 'R1', 'r', 'R2' at the far end
faint concentric circle outlines on the far end cap showing the two conductor radii
central axis line of the coaxial assembly

interactions.label: Gaussian radius r
interactions.teaches: As r grows within the gap, the same enclosed charge +Q spreads over a larger cylindrical area, so E ∝ 1/r — the red arrows at the dashed surface shorten while the enclosed charge readout stays fixed.

interactions.label: Region
interactions.teaches: Where charge is enclosed and where the field exists: zero inside the conductor, E = λ/(2πε₀r) in the annular gap, and zero outside because the enclosed charge is +Q − Q = 0.
The coaxial nesting of the three surfaces — the dashed Gaussian cylinder truly lies between the two conductors along the whole length, not just at the end faces.

demo_steps.title: The coaxial geometry
demo_steps.narration: An inner cylinder of radius R1 carrying +Q sits inside an outer shell of radius R2 carrying −Q. Red arrows in the gap show the radial field pointing from + to −.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the Gaussian surface toward R1
demo_steps.narration: Move the dashed cylinder close to the inner conductor. The enclosed charge is unchanged, but the surface area 2πrL is smaller, so E at the surface is large — the arrows lengthen.

demo_steps.title: Expand toward R2
demo_steps.narration: Push the dashed cylinder out to just inside the outer shell. Same enclosed +Q, larger area, so E falls off as 1/r and the arrows shorten.

demo_steps.title: Inside the inner conductor
demo_steps.narration: Choose r < R1: the Gaussian cylinder encloses no charge, so the flux and the field are zero inside the conductor.

demo_steps.title: Outside the capacitor
demo_steps.narration: Choose r > R2: the surface now encloses +Q and −Q together. Net enclosed charge is zero, so no field escapes the capacitor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axis along +X (screen-right and slightly receding). Length L = 10 units, drawn from near end at x = −5 (lower-left, larger on screen) to far end at x = +5 (upper-right). Inner conductor radius R1 = 1.0; outer shell radius R2 = 3.0, shell wall thickness ~0.15. Gaussian dashed cylinder radius r default 2.0, slider range 1.0–3.0 for the gap (extended 0.3–3.8 when the region toggle allows inside/outside). Colors: outer shell translucent lavender-grey #C6CBE0 with lighter highlight band along the top (#E8EAF3) and darker rim face #9AA1BF; inner cylinder same family slightly darker; '+' and '−' signs dark navy #2B2F4A, '+' on the inner cylinder face and along its length, '−' scattered on the outer shell surface (roughly 7 along the top and 7 along the bottom of the length, plus ~14 around the near rim); red E arrows #E03A2F, ~12 arrows radiating in the near-end plane from r = R1 to r = R2, arrowheads outward; Gaussian surface orange dashed #F0A030, dash length ~0.25. Near end is cut away so the inner cylinder face and the annular gap are visible; the far end shows faint concentric circles. Far-end radius arrows all emanate from the axis point at x = +5 and fan into the upper-right quadrant: R1 shortest (nearly vertical, length 1.0), r intermediate (about 45° up-right, length r), R2 longest (about 30° below horizontal to the right, length 3.0). 'Gaussian surface' text sits at the top center-right of the frame with a curved black leader sweeping down-left to touch the top dashed line about 55% along its length. E = λ/(2πε₀r) for R1 < r < R2, zero elsewhere; C = 2πε₀L / ln(R2/R1).
interactionPlan.notes: Build cylinders with THREE.CylinderGeometry rotated to the X axis; use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transparent:true, opacity ~0.45, depthWrite:false and side:DoubleSide for the outer shell so the inner cylinder and arrows read through it. Render the outer shell as an open-ended tube plus a separate ring (RingGeometry) for the near annular face to produce the cutaway look. Dashed Gaussian surface: LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) for two end ellipses (EllipseCurve points) and two straight generatrices along the top and bottom silhouette; drive its radius from the slider by rebuilding or scaling the line geometry in Y/Z. E arrows as ArrowHelper instances in the near-end plane, length and color intensity scaled by 1/r; hide them entirely when region is 'inside' or 'outside'. '+' and '−' glyphs as small sprite/canvas textures billboarded toward the camera so they stay legible while orbiting. Labels E, R1, r, R2 and 'Gaussian surface' as CSS2DRenderer HTML labels anchored to world points; the curved leader as a QuadraticBezierCurve3 tube or Line with a small cone arrowhead. Highlight the active region with a translucent colored shell (green tint for the active zone) toggled by the region control, and show a small readout of Q_enclosed and E magnitude.

authoredContext:
A cylindrical capacitor consists of two concentric, conducting cylinders (the figure). The inner cylinder, of radius R1, may either be a shell or be completely solid. The outer cylinder is a shell of inner radius R2. We assume that the length of each cylinder is l and that the excess charges +Q and −Q reside on the inner and outer cylinders, respectively.

With edge effects ignored, the electrical field between the conductors is directed radially outward from the common axis of the cylinders. Using the Gaussian surface shown in the figure, we have

A cylindrical capacitor consists of two concentric, conducting cylinders. Here, the charge on the outer surface of the inner cylinder is positive (indicated by +) and the charge on the inner surface of the outer cylinder is negative (indicated by −).

Figure shows two concentric cylinders. The inner one, with radius R1 has positive signs on it. The outer one, with radius R2 has negative signs on it. Arrows marked E are shown radiating from the inner one to the outer one. A third cylinder, with radius r, is shown as a dotted line between the two. This is labeled Gaussian surface.

discrepancies: Camera/orientation: the source is a near-axonometric side view with the far end cap turned toward the viewer so the R₁ / r / R₂ radius arrows read clearly; the generated view rotates the tube so the far cap faces away and is strongly foreshortened, burying the black radius arrows and their labels inside the shell.

Color scheme diverges: source is a uniform lavender/blue-grey metallic tube with bright orange dashed Gaussian lines; the generated figure is mostly white/grey with a prominent green translucent Gaussian shell, and the dashed orange contour reads as faint olive, losing the figure's signature orange annotation.

The '−' charge glyphs on the outer shell (two long rows along the top and bottom plus the ring of minus signs on the near rim) are barely visible in the render, whereas they are a prominent element of the source.

Labels 'E', 'R₁', 'r', 'R₂' are effectively unreadable at the default framing (tiny and/or behind geometry); only the small 'Gaussian surface' callout is discernible, and even it is much smaller relative to the figure than in the source.
The translucent green/grey volumetric Gaussian cylinder is an addition not present in the source (which shows only a dashed wireframe surface) and it visually dominates the interior.

Source shows a distinct pale highlight band along the top of the tube and concentric faint circles on the far cap; these are present in code but essentially invisible, flattening the tube's shading compared to the source.
evaluation.notes: Topologically correct coaxial-capacitor Gauss's-law figure with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (radius slider, region buttons with correct E=0/1-r physics, guided demo, display toggles), but the rotated viewpoint hides the far-end radius annotations, the palette drifts to white/grey-plus-green instead of lavender/orange, and the key labels are too small to read.
action_items: Set the camera closer to the source vantage (azimuth so the far end cap with R₁/r/R₂ is visible, slight elevation, near-orthographic/axonometric) so the radius arrows and their labels are unoccluded.

Restore the source palette: lavender-blue shell and inner conductor, saturated orange for the dashed Gaussian lines (increase linewidth/contrast), and either remove or greatly desaturate the green volumetric Gaussian shell.

Increase label font sizes (e.g. 18–20px for E, R₁, r, R₂ and a bolder 'Gaussian surface' callout) and offset R-labels outward so they sit beside their arrows rather than inside the tube; darken/enlarge the '−' and '+' glyph sprites so the charge distribution is legible.
Make the near-rim '−' ring and top/bottom '−' rows render in front of the translucent shell (adjust renderOrder/depthTest) so they read as in the source.
plan_action_items: Specify a front-left axonometric camera matching the source (far cap visible) rather than a rotated perspective view, since the R₁/r/R₂ annotation cluster lives on the far end.
Plan the Gaussian surface as a dashed wireframe only (ellipses + generatrices) with at most a very faint tint, to match the source's annotation style.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional cutaway of a cylindrical capacitor drawn in perspective, extending from the near end at the lower left toward the far end at the upper right. Two concentric conducting cylinders share a common axis: a narrow inner cylinder whose visible near face is crowded with plus signs, and a much wider outer shell whose surface carries minus signs spaced along its length and around its near rim. In the near end view, short red arrows labeled 'E' radiate outward from the inner cylinder across the annular gap to the inner wall of the outer shell, filling the gap uniformly in every radial direction. An orange dashed cylinder of intermediate radius is drawn between the two conductors, appearing as dashed ellipses at both ends joined by dashed lines running the length of the device; a curved leader from the top labels it 'Gaussian surface'. At the far end three arrows fan out from a point on the axis, labeled 'R1', 'r', and 'R2' in order of increasing length. Nesting the dashed surface between the two conductor radii shows precisely which charge it encloses. The geometry sets up the flux calculation that gives the capacitance of a coaxial pair carrying charges plus Q and minus Q.

Color scheme diverges: the source is a cool lavender/blue-violet shell with saturated red arrows and navy +/− glyphs; the render reads grey/tan-brown with washed-out pink-red arrows and pale blue-grey charge glyphs.

Perspective is much stronger than the source's near-orthographic side view, so the cylinder tapers dramatically and the inner conductor (radius R₁ with its dense '+' cap) is barely distinguishable from the shell interior.
The '−' glyphs are rendered with depthTest off, so several float outside the shell silhouette at the left edge, detached from the outer conductor surface they should mark.
Text annotations (E, 'Gaussian surface', R₁, r, R₂) are rendered much smaller relative to the figure than in the source, where they are prominent; R₁/r/R₂ are nearly illegible at the default framing.
The near-end red E arrows stay visible in the 'Inside conductor' and 'Outside' regions where the readout states E = 0, which conflicts with the stated result.
evaluation.notes: All the source elements (coaxial conductors, +/− charges, radial E arrows, dashed Gaussian cylinder, radius callouts, leader squiggle) are present with an excellent set of meaningful interactions and a guided demo, but the camera flips near/far so the cutaway face is in the distance, the palette drifts from lavender/red to grey/washed pink, and the labels are too small to read comfortably.

feedback.rationale: All conceptual elements and interactions are correct; the issues are execution-level (camera orientation/perspective, palette, label sizing, depth-test glyph bleed, arrow visibility gating) that can be fixed in rendering.

interactions.label: Gaussian radius r
interactions.teaches: As r grows within the gap, the same enclosed charge +Q spreads over a larger cylindrical area, so E ∝ 1/r — the red arrows at the dashed surface shorten while the enclosed charge readout stays fixed.

interactions.label: Region
interactions.teaches: Where charge is enclosed and where the field exists: zero inside the conductor, E = λ/(2πε₀r) in the annular gap, and zero outside because the enclosed charge is +Q − Q = 0.
The coaxial nesting of the three surfaces — the dashed Gaussian cylinder truly lies between the two conductors along the whole length, not just at the end faces.

demo_steps.title: The coaxial geometry
demo_steps.narration: An inner cylinder of radius R1 carrying +Q sits inside an outer shell of radius R2 carrying −Q. Red arrows in the gap show the radial field pointing from + to −.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the Gaussian surface toward R1
demo_steps.narration: Move the dashed cylinder close to the inner conductor. The enclosed charge is unchanged, but the surface area 2πrL is smaller, so E at the surface is large — the arrows lengthen.

demo_steps.title: Expand toward R2
demo_steps.narration: Push the dashed cylinder out to just inside the outer shell. Same enclosed +Q, larger area, so E falls off as 1/r and the arrows shorten.

demo_steps.title: Inside the inner conductor
demo_steps.narration: Choose r < R1: the Gaussian cylinder encloses no charge, so the flux and the field are zero inside the conductor.

demo_steps.title: Outside the capacitor
demo_steps.narration: Choose r > R2: the surface now encloses +Q and −Q together. Net enclosed charge is zero, so no field escapes the capacitor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Axis along +X (screen-right and slightly receding). Length L = 10 units, drawn from near end at x = −5 (lower-left, larger on screen) to far end at x = +5 (upper-right). Inner conductor radius R1 = 1.0; outer shell radius R2 = 3.0, shell wall thickness ~0.15. Gaussian dashed cylinder radius r default 2.0, slider range 1.0–3.0 for the gap (extended 0.3–3.8 when the region toggle allows inside/outside). Colors: outer shell translucent lavender-grey #C6CBE0 with lighter highlight band along the top (#E8EAF3) and darker rim face #9AA1BF; inner cylinder same family slightly darker; '+' and '−' signs dark navy #2B2F4A, '+' on the inner cylinder face and along its length, '−' scattered on the outer shell surface (roughly 7 along the top and 7 along the bottom of the length, plus ~14 around the near rim); red E arrows #E03A2F, ~12 arrows radiating in the near-end plane from r = R1 to r = R2, arrowheads outward; Gaussian surface orange dashed #F0A030, dash length ~0.25. Near end is cut away so the inner cylinder face and the annular gap are visible; the far end shows faint concentric circles. Far-end radius arrows all emanate from the axis point at x = +5 and fan into the upper-right quadrant: R1 shortest (nearly vertical, length 1.0), r intermediate (about 45° up-right, length r), R2 longest (about 30° below horizontal to the right, length 3.0). 'Gaussian surface' text sits at the top center-right of the frame with a curved black leader sweeping down-left to touch the top dashed line about 55% along its length. E = λ/(2πε₀r) for R1 < r < R2, zero elsewhere; C = 2πε₀L / ln(R2/R1).
interactionPlan.notes: Build cylinders with THREE.CylinderGeometry rotated to the X axis; use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transparent:true, opacity ~0.45, depthWrite:false and side:DoubleSide for the outer shell so the inner cylinder and arrows read through it. Render the outer shell as an open-ended tube plus a separate ring (RingGeometry) for the near annular face to produce the cutaway look. Dashed Gaussian surface: LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) for two end ellipses (EllipseCurve points) and two straight generatrices along the top and bottom silhouette; drive its radius from the slider by rebuilding or scaling the line geometry in Y/Z. E arrows as ArrowHelper instances in the near-end plane, length and color intensity scaled by 1/r; hide them entirely when region is 'inside' or 'outside'. '+' and '−' glyphs as small sprite/canvas textures billboarded toward the camera so they stay legible while orbiting. Labels E, R1, r, R2 and 'Gaussian surface' as CSS2DRenderer HTML labels anchored to world points; the curved leader as a QuadraticBezierCurve3 tube or Line with a small cone arrowhead. Highlight the active region with a translucent colored shell (green tint for the active zone) toggled by the region control, and show a small readout of Q_enclosed and E magnitude.

discrepancies: The cut-away near end is viewed nearly edge-on: in the source the left face is a broad ellipse where the annulus, the crowded '+' charges and the 12 red radial arrows read clearly, while in the generated view they collapse into a narrow vertical smear of overlapping red arrows at the left edge.

The inner conductor (radius R₁) is barely distinguishable in the generated figure — in the source it is a clearly separate small cylinder with a visible near face full of '+' signs and its own outline running the length of the tube.
Extra radial E-field arrows have been added at mid-length on the Gaussian cylinder; the source shows red arrows only in the cut-away end plane.

Color/tonal match is weaker: the source's saturated lavender-to-blue-grey shaded body reads as a solid metallic tube, whereas the generated shell is very washed-out/near-white with an orange tint from the Gaussian volume, losing the shell/inner-cylinder contrast.

Charge glyphs along the body are placed loosely in the interior volume rather than on the outer shell surface rows and the inner cylinder surface as in the source, so the '+' row appears to float mid-gap.
evaluation.notes: All the right elements (coaxial cylinders, cut-away end, red radial E arrows, orange dashed Gaussian cylinder, R₁/r/R₂ callouts, leader-annotated caption) are present with excellent, physics-correct interactions, but the chosen azimuth foreshortens the cut-away near face so the signature radial arrow rosette and inner conductor become an unreadable clump, and the pastel shading is washed out relative to the source.
action_items: Rotate the camera (reduce azimuth toward ~135–150° off-axis, or increase the yaw so the near end face is seen as a wide ellipse) so the cut-away annulus, its '+' charges and the 12 red radial arrows are clearly legible as in the source.
Increase opacity/saturation of the outer shell and inner cylinder gradients and add a visible inner-cylinder silhouette line along the length so the two conductors and the gap are distinguishable.
Anchor the '+' glyphs on the inner cylinder surface and '−' glyphs on the outer shell top/bottom silhouettes so they do not appear to float in the gap volume.
Consider hiding (or making toggle-only) the mid-length surface E arrows so the default view matches the source, which shows field arrows only on the cut face.
plan_action_items: Specify the default viewpoint explicitly as a three-quarter view with the cut-away end face presented as a broad ellipse (source-matching), rather than a near edge-on perspective.
